we have developed a new unfolding algorithm for correlated noise in the TileCal photomultipliers and we have shown that the correlated component can be reduced to negligible values for pedestal runs and in the presence of signals like minimum bias and top quark pair events.
the correlated noise is reduced and unfolded by the proposed algorithm and that this is achieved for pedestal runs, as well as for physics events.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study and removal of correlated noise on the TileCal detector, which is the barrel hadronic sampling calorimeter of the LHC experiment ATLAS.
the understanding of the response of the calorimeters of the ATLAS detector to minimum bias events, top quark pair events, and to the correlated noise component of the calorimeter response.
the study of correlated noise on TileCal, the ATLAS barrel hadronic calorimetre, and the development of an algorithm to unfold it from the signal.

the correlated noise can be removed from the photomultiplier response and that the unfolding algorithm can be applied to the response of the calorimeter.
the correlated noise can be unfolded from the response of a hadronic calorimetre, and that the resulting signal can be used to perform physics analysis with a negligible effect on the final results.
the correlated noise is well described by the model, and the unfolding algorithm can successfully remove the noise in the calorimeter signals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the correlated noise is not a problem for the ATLAS detector.
we have shown that it is possible to reduce the correlated noise component to a level that it does not significantly affect the response of the calorimeter to the physics signals.

we have successfully parametrized, unfolded and reduced the correlated noise component of the TileCal photomultipliers, and the results of this study are used for the calibration of the TileCal response in the ATLAS data.

the unfolding algorithm can be used to correct the response of the calorimeter in the presence of noise, which can be used in the future for the calibration of the calorimeter response in the presence of a signal, and for the estimation of the systematic uncertainties on the calibration.
it is feasible to unfold correlated noise from the response of a calorimeter, and that the unfolded response is more accurate.
